En 1642, à Rouen, Blaise Pascal a 19 ans: In 1642, in Rouen, Blaise Pascal is 19. His father, in charge of the province's taxes, is buried under additions. Blaise builds him a machine: toothed wheels that carry the digits, and a small part, the jumper, that drops to pass the carry to the next wheel. It will take him some fifty prototypes and three years to present it.
Un jeune homme invente une machine pour: A young man invents a machine to spare his father the arithmetic. You won't even do your own.
Le 21 juin 1948, à l'université de Manch: On June 21, 1948, at the University of Manchester, a small machine cobbled together by Freddie Williams, Tom Kilburn and Geoff Tootill runs a program stored in its own memory, on the screen of a cathode-ray tube. It looks for the largest divisor of a number. It is the first time a machine reads its program from its electronic memory, just like its data.
Une machine qui garde son programme en m: A machine that keeps its program in memory. Which is more than you do with your lessons.
